players.name: Lionel Messi
players.bio: Widely regarded as one of the greatest football players of all time, Messi spent the majority of his professional career at Barcelona, winning a record 8 Ballon d'Or awards and leading Argentina to World Cup glory in 2022.
players.style: Known for his low center of gravity, extraordinary close control dribbling, vision, and prolific finishing. Messi operates as a winger, false 9, or central playmaker, using his acceleration and passing range to dictate play and unlock defenses.

timeline.title: Barcelona Debut
timeline.description: Made his official first-team debut for FC Barcelona at age 17.

timeline.title: Sextuple & First Ballon d'Or
timeline.description: Won all six club competitions in a calendar year with Barca, claiming his first Ballon d'Or.

timeline.title: 91-Goal Record
timeline.description: Broke the calendar year goalscoring record, netting 91 goals in all competitions.

timeline.title: Copa América Champion
timeline.description: Led Argentina to their first major international title in 28 years.

timeline.title: World Cup Victory
timeline.description: Won the FIFA World Cup in Qatar, claiming the tournament's Golden Ball award.

players.name: Cristiano Ronaldo
players.bio: An absolute powerhouse of modern football, Ronaldo has won 5 Ballon d'Or awards and holds the records for most goals scored in the Champions League, European Championship, and international football.
players.style: Ronaldo transitioned from a tricky, lightning-fast winger to a physically dominant, elite goalscoring striker. He combines explosive athleticism, aerial ability, and lethal finishing with both feet.

timeline.title: Manchester United Transfer
timeline.description: Joined Manchester United from Sporting CP, inheriting the iconic #7 shirt.

timeline.title: First Champions League & Ballon d'Or
timeline.description: Scored in the UCL Final victory and claimed his first Ballon d'Or.

timeline.title: Real Madrid Move
timeline.description: Joined Real Madrid for a world-record fee, going on to score 450 goals in 438 matches.

timeline.title: Euro 2016 Glory
timeline.description: Captained Portugal to their first-ever major international trophy in France.

timeline.title: International Goals Record
timeline.description: Solidified his place as the top international goalscorer of all time.

players.name: Kylian Mbappé
players.bio: One of the most exciting talents of his generation, Mbappé burst onto the scene as a teenager and won the FIFA World Cup in 2018, scoring in the final at age 19. At the 2026 World Cup he became the tournament's all-time top scorer with 22 goals.
players.style: Possesses devastating pace, quick dribbling, and lethal composure in 1v1 situations. Mbappé thrives on exploiting high defensive lines, cutting inside from the left wing to curl shots into the far corner.

timeline.title: Monaco Breakthrough
timeline.description: Helped Monaco win the Ligue 1 title and reach the Champions League semi-finals.

timeline.title: Paris Saint-Germain Transfer
timeline.description: Joined PSG in a historic deal, becoming the club's all-time record goalscorer.

timeline.title: World Cup Triumph
timeline.description: Won the World Cup with France, claiming the Best Young Player award.

timeline.title: World Cup Final Hat-Trick
timeline.description: Scored a historic hat-trick in the World Cup Final, winning the Golden Boot.

timeline.title: Real Madrid Signing
timeline.description: Completed his highly-anticipated transfer to Real Madrid.

timeline.title: World Cup Scoring Record
timeline.description: Won a second straight Golden Boot with 10 goals, passing Miroslav Klose and Lionel Messi as the World Cup's all-time top scorer.

players.name: Pelé
players.bio: Edson Arantes do Nascimento, known globally as Pelé, is widely considered the king of football. He remains the only player in history to win three FIFA World Cups.
players.style: An athletic and complete forward who could shoot with both feet, head the ball with power, and execute breathtaking dribbles. Pelé's vision, playmaking abilities, and clinical scoring revolutionized the game.

timeline.title: Santos FC Debut
timeline.description: Made his debut for Santos at age 15, scoring in his first match.

timeline.title: First World Cup at 17
timeline.description: Became the youngest player to win the World Cup, scoring twice in the final.

timeline.title: Second World Cup Win
timeline.description: Won back-to-back titles with Brazil, establishing them as global giants.

timeline.title: Legendary 1970 Campaign
timeline.description: Led what is considered the greatest team in history to win his third World Cup.

timeline.title: New York Cosmos Move
timeline.description: Joined the NASL to popularize football in the United States.

players.name: Andrés Iniesta
players.bio: The midfield maestro who scored the winning goal in the 2010 World Cup Final. Iniesta was the central heartbeat of Barcelona and Spain's golden eras of dominant possession football.
players.style: An elegant, agile playmaker whose trademark move was 'La Croqueta'. He excelled in tight spaces, possessing unmatched balance, spatial awareness, and passing accuracy to control the midfield tempo.

timeline.title: Barcelona Debut
timeline.description: Rose through La Masia to make his first-team debut under Louis van Gaal.

timeline.title: Euro 2008 Champions
timeline.description: Named in the Team of the Tournament as Spain won the European Championship.

timeline.title: Iniestazo at Stamford Bridge
timeline.description: Scored a legendary last-minute goal against Chelsea to send Barca to the UCL Final.

timeline.title: World Cup Winning Goal
timeline.description: Scored the historic 116th-minute winner against the Netherlands in South Africa.

timeline.title: Euro 2012 Best Player
timeline.description: Won the UEFA Best Player in Europe award after leading Spain to back-to-back Euros.

players.name: Franz Beckenbauer
players.bio: Nicknamed 'Der Kaiser' (The Emperor), Beckenbauer is credited with inventing the modern 'Libero' (sweeper) role. He won the World Cup as both a captain and a manager.
players.style: Commanding, elegant, and tactically supreme. Beckenbauer would drop behind the defense to clean up play, then carry the ball forward with grace to join the midfield, launching attacks from deep.

timeline.title: Bayern Munich Debut
timeline.description: Made his debut for Bayern Munich, transforming them into a European superpower.

timeline.title: Ballon d'Or & Euro 72
timeline.description: Captained West Germany to Euro glory and won his first Ballon d'Or.

timeline.title: World Cup Captain
timeline.description: Led West Germany to lift the World Cup on home soil, defeating Cruyff's Netherlands.

timeline.title: UCL Three-Peat
timeline.description: Captained Bayern Munich to their third consecutive European Cup title.

timeline.title: World Cup Winner as Manager
timeline.description: Managed West Germany to a World Cup victory in Italy, joining a rare elite club.

players.name: Diego Maradona
players.bio: One of the most iconic figures in sports history, Maradona was a footballing genius who single-handedly inspired Argentina to the 1986 World Cup and transformed Napoli into Serie A champions.
players.style: A master dribbler with magical footwork, balance, and crossing ability. Maradona used his legendary left foot to execute free kicks, defense-splitting passes, and solo runs that defined a generation.

timeline.title: Professional Debut at 15
timeline.description: Debuted for Argentinos Juniors ten days before his 16th birthday.

timeline.title: Barcelona Transfer
timeline.description: Joined Barcelona for a world-record fee, winning the Copa del Rey.

timeline.title: Napoli Revolution
timeline.description: Transferred to Napoli, leading them to their only two Serie A titles in history (1987, 1990).

timeline.title: The Goal of the Century
timeline.description: Scored the famous 'Hand of God' and the 60-meter solo 'Goal of the Century' against England.

timeline.title: World Cup Runner-up
timeline.description: Led Argentina to a second consecutive World Cup Final, falling to West Germany.

players.name: Zinedine Zidane
players.bio: An icon of elegance and big-match performance, Zidane scored twice in the 1998 World Cup Final and went on to win three Champions League titles in a row as the manager of Real Madrid.
players.style: Zidane was characterized by his ball control, body feints, vision, and technical precision. He possessed the rare ability to make complex movements look completely effortless.

timeline.title: Juventus Move
timeline.description: Joined Juventus from Bordeaux, winning back-to-back Serie A titles.

timeline.title: World Cup & Ballon d'Or
timeline.description: Scored two headers in the final against Brazil to win the World Cup, claiming the Ballon d'Or.

timeline.title: Galáctico Transfer
timeline.description: Joined Real Madrid for a world-record transfer fee.

timeline.title: Legendary UCL Volley
timeline.description: Scored one of the greatest goals in history—a left-foot volley in the UCL Final.

timeline.title: World Cup Final & Retirement
timeline.description: Led France to the final, winning the Golden Ball before retiring from professional play.

coaches.name: Pep Guardiola
coaches.bio: Famous for his obsessive tactical perfectionism and high-possession style, Guardiola revolutionized modern football at Barcelona, Bayern Munich, and Manchester City.
coaches.style: Guardiola is the leading advocate of 'Juego de Posición' (Positional Play). His teams utilize short passes, extreme high press, building out from the goalkeeper, and using inverted fullbacks or defenders stepping into midfield to create central overloads.

timeline.title: Barcelona Appointment
timeline.description: Promoted to first-team manager, shifting the squad towards a possession-heavy style.

timeline.title: Historic Sextuple
timeline.description: Won all six available club trophies in his debut season, a football first.

timeline.title: Bayern Munich Project
timeline.description: Brought his possession style to Germany, winning three Bundesliga titles in a row.

timeline.title: Centurions Season
timeline.description: Led Manchester City to a record-breaking 100 points in the Premier League.

timeline.title: Treble Victory
timeline.description: Won the Champions League, Premier League, and FA Cup in a historic campaign.

timeline.title: Manchester City Farewell
timeline.description: Left City after a decade and 20 trophies, signing off with a domestic cup double.

coaches.name: José Mourinho
coaches.bio: One of the most successful and controversial managers in history, 'The Special One' is famous for his defensive masterclasses, tactical discipline, and winning titles in four different leagues.
coaches.style: Mourinho focuses on absolute defensive organization, compact low blocks, and lethal fast transition attacks. He prioritizes structural safety, letting the opponent have the ball while closing all spaces, then exploiting turnovers.

timeline.title: Porto UCL Miracle
timeline.description: Led underdog Porto to win the UEFA Champions League, earning international acclaim.

timeline.title: Chelsea Premier League Title
timeline.description: Won the Premier League in his first season, conceding a record-low 15 goals.

timeline.title: Inter Milan Treble
timeline.description: Won Serie A, Coppa Italia, and UCL, defeating Bayern Munich in the final.

timeline.title: Real Madrid La Liga Title
timeline.description: Broke the La Liga points (100) and goals (121) records to defeat Guardiola's Barca.

timeline.title: Roma Conference League Win
timeline.description: Became the first manager to win all three current UEFA club competitions.

timeline.title: Real Madrid Return
timeline.description: Returned to the Bernabéu for a second spell, 13 years after his first.

coaches.name: Jürgen Klopp
coaches.bio: Known for his charismatic leadership and explosive, fast-tempo football, Klopp resurrected Borussia Dortmund and Liverpool, guiding them to domestic and European glory. In July 2026 he became head coach of Germany.
coaches.style: Klopp operates under the 'Heavy Metal Football' style, utilizing high-intensity Gegenpressing (counter-pressing). His teams immediately press the ball upon losing possession, looking to create quick vertical attack transitions.

timeline.title: Mainz Bundesliga Promotion
timeline.description: Guided Mainz to the Bundesliga for the first time in their history.

timeline.title: Dortmund Bundesliga Champion
timeline.description: Won the Bundesliga title with an energetic, young squad, repeating in 2012.

timeline.title: Champions League Winner
timeline.description: Won Liverpool's sixth European Cup, defeating Tottenham in the Madrid final.

timeline.title: Premier League Champion
timeline.description: Led Liverpool to their first league title in 30 years with 99 points.

timeline.title: Liverpool Farewell
timeline.description: Concluded his legendary tenure at Anfield, winning the EFL Cup in his final season.

timeline.title: Germany Head Coach
timeline.description: Appointed Germany head coach after the 2026 World Cup, on a deal running to the 2030 World Cup.

coaches.name: Arsène Wenger
coaches.bio: Nicknamed 'Le Professeur', Wenger spent 22 years at Arsenal, introducing innovative training methods, nutrition, and scouting to English football.
coaches.style: Wenger advocated for fluid, free-flowing, attacking football with creative players rotating positions. He trusted in technical mastery, intelligent off-the-ball movements, and fast combination passes.

timeline.title: Monaco Ligue 1 Champion
timeline.description: Won the French league title in his debut season with Monaco.

timeline.title: Arsenal Appointment
timeline.description: Joined Arsenal as a relatively unknown French manager, quickly transforming the club.

timeline.title: First Premier League Double
timeline.description: Won the Premier League and FA Cup double in his first full season.

timeline.title: The Invincibles
timeline.description: Achieved the legendary unbeaten Premier League season (26 wins, 12 draws).

timeline.title: Arsenal Retirement
timeline.description: Concluded his historic 22-year reign at Arsenal as their most successful manager.

coaches.name: Diego Simeone
coaches.bio: Famous for his intense touchline energy, Diego 'El Cholo' Simeone broke the Barcelona-Real Madrid duopoly in Spain, transforming Atletico Madrid into a defensive juggernaut.
coaches.style: Simeone's philosophy ('Cholismo') relies on a compact, disciplined 4-4-2 low/mid block, extreme aggression, defensive solidarity, and vertical counter-attacks. He treats tactical discipline and team unity as paramount.

timeline.title: Atletico Madrid Appointment
timeline.description: Took over a struggling Atletico team, immediately instilling defensive discipline.

timeline.title: Europa League Success
timeline.description: Won the UEFA Europa League in his first half-season, defeating Athletic Bilbao.

timeline.title: La Liga Champions
timeline.description: Broke the Real-Barca duopoly, winning the league and reaching the UCL Final.

timeline.title: Second Europa League
timeline.description: Won his second Europa League title with a 3-0 victory over Marseille.

timeline.title: Second La Liga Triumph
timeline.description: Won his second La Liga title, adapting the team into a flexible defensive system.

coaches.name: Luiz Felipe Scolari
coaches.bio: Nicknamed 'Big Phil', Scolari is a legendary Brazilian manager who led Brazil to their fifth World Cup title in 2002 and managed teams across Europe, South America, and Asia.
coaches.style: Scolari emphasizes the 'Familia Scolari' (family bond) to build team spirit. Tactically, he blends solid defensive screens (typically defensive midfielders) with immense individual attacking freedom for creative stars.

timeline.title: Copa Libertadores Winner
timeline.description: Won the South American championship with Gremio, repeating in 1999 with Palmeiras.

timeline.title: World Cup Glory
timeline.description: Led Brazil's iconic team to win all 7 matches in South Korea/Japan, claiming their 5th World Cup.

timeline.title: Euro 2004 Runner-up
timeline.description: Managed Portugal to the final of Euro 2004, losing narrowly to Greece.

timeline.title: World Cup 4th Place
timeline.description: Led Portugal to their best World Cup finish in 40 years, reaching the semi-finals.

timeline.title: Confederations Cup Win
timeline.description: Returned to Brazil, defeating Spain 3-0 in the final.

teams.name: Argentina
teams.bio: Argentina has a rich footballing history defined by passion, supreme individual talent, and tactical innovation. The home of Diego Maradona and Lionel Messi, La Albiceleste has captured the world's imagination for generations.
teams.tacticalIdentity: Historically, Argentine football revolves around 'La Nuestra'—a style emphasizing high technical skill, dribbling, and creativity. Modern systems blend this traditional flair with aggressive counter-pressing and structured defensive support to liberate their creative playmakers.

timeline.title: First World Cup Title
timeline.description: Won the tournament on home soil, led by top scorer Mario Kempes.

timeline.title: Maradona's Masterpiece
timeline.description: Diego Maradona captained Argentina to a second World Cup in Mexico with legendary performances.

timeline.title: Copa América Triumph
timeline.description: Defeated Brazil in Rio to end a 28-year senior international trophy drought.

timeline.title: Third Star in Qatar
timeline.description: Lionel Messi led La Albiceleste to World Cup glory in one of the greatest finals ever played.

teams.name: Brazil
teams.bio: The most successful national team in World Cup history, Brazil is synonymous with 'Jogo Bonito' (The Beautiful Game). A factory of footballing wizards from Pelé to Ronaldinho, Brazil represents the absolute peak of footballing joy.
teams.tacticalIdentity: Brazil's footballing identity is built on samba-like rhythm, individual expression, fluid wingplay, and attacking fullbacks. It focuses on numerical overloads, high technical skills, and encouraging players to take creative risks in 1v1 situations.

timeline.title: Pelé Emerges in Sweden
timeline.description: A 17-year-old Pelé led Brazil to their first World Cup, introducing Jogo Bonito to the world.

timeline.title: The Perfect Team
timeline.description: Brazil won their third World Cup with what is widely considered the greatest football team ever assembled.

timeline.title: Tetra in USA
timeline.description: Defeated Italy on penalties after a defensive, structured tournament led by Romário.

timeline.title: Pentacampeão in Asia
timeline.description: The 'R' trio of Ronaldo, Rivaldo, and Ronaldinho swept the tournament to win Brazil's fifth star.

teams.name: France
teams.bio: France (Les Bleus) has risen to become a dominant powerhouse of modern football. Blessed with incredible multi-cultural diversity and world-class academies, France blends physical dominance with supreme technical elegance.
teams.tacticalIdentity: Under Didier Deschamps, France focuses on a highly organized defensive shape, minimizing risk in possession, and utilizing lightning-fast counter-attacks through explosive wingers like Kylian Mbappé.

timeline.title: Platini's Euro Domination
timeline.description: Michel Platini scored a record 9 goals in 5 games to secure France's first European Championship.

timeline.title: First World Cup Star
timeline.description: Zidane scored twice in Paris as the host nation defeated Brazil 3-0 in the final.

timeline.title: Double Champions
timeline.description: Won Euro 2000 with a golden goal from David Trezeguet, completing a rare double.

timeline.title: Glory in Russia
timeline.description: A young, explosive French team defeated Croatia 4-2 in Moscow to claim their second World Cup.

teams.name: Germany
teams.bio: Germany (Die Mannschaft) is the epitome of tournament resilience, tactical intelligence, and collective strength. Always competing at the business end of tournaments, German football blends robust physical structure with modern positional play.
teams.tacticalIdentity: German football has transitioned from powerful physical efficiency to dynamic positional play. Their style emphasizes occupying half-spaces, high pressing, and intelligent player movement (like the 'Raumdeuter' or space investigator).

timeline.title: The Miracle of Bern
timeline.description: Dealt the legendary Hungarian 'Golden Team' their first defeat in 4 years to win their 1st World Cup.

timeline.title: Beckenbauer's Triumph
timeline.description: Der Kaiser captained Germany to victory on home soil, defeating Cruyff's Total Football.

timeline.title: Matthäus Captains Unified Germany
timeline.description: Defeated Maradona's Argentina in Rome just before the formal reunification of Germany.

timeline.title: Historic 7-1 & Fourth Star
timeline.description: Swept past hosts Brazil 7-1 in the semi-final before Mario Götze's extra-time goal won the final.

teams.name: Spain
teams.bio: Spain (La Roja) defined an entire era of modern football with 'Tiki-Taka'. Built upon the technical superiority of small, creative midfielders and a commitment to possession, Spain dominated international football from 2008 to 2012.
teams.tacticalIdentity: Tiki-Taka focuses on absolute possession, short rapid passing, triangular movements, and constant rotation of midfielders. The philosophy believes that if the opponent doesn't have the ball, they cannot score.

timeline.title: Euro 2008 Triumph
timeline.description: Broke decades of underachievement by defeating Germany in Vienna under Luis Aragonés.

timeline.title: World Cup Glory
timeline.description: Andrés Iniesta scored the extra-time winner against the Netherlands to claim Spain's first World Cup.

timeline.title: Historic Treble
timeline.description: Defeated Italy 4-0 in the Euro 2012 final, completing an unprecedented consecutive three major title run.

timeline.title: Euro 2024 Champions
timeline.description: Won every single game in Germany to win their record-breaking 4th European Championship.

teams.name: Portugal
teams.bio: Portugal (Seleção das Quinas) has consistently punched above its weight, developing some of the most gifted wingers and forwards in history, including Eusébio, Luís Figo, and Cristiano Ronaldo.
teams.tacticalIdentity: Portuguese football combines solid tactical discipline and defensive blocks with highly explosive, creative attacking transitions. Players focus on technical dribbling, tactical intelligence, and exploiting spaces via quick wing attacks.

timeline.title: Eusébio's Bronze Campaign
timeline.description: Eusébio led Portugal to a third-place finish in their debut World Cup, scoring 9 goals.

timeline.title: Euro 2004 Heartbreak
timeline.description: Reached the final on home soil but suffered a shock 1-0 defeat to underdogs Greece.

timeline.title: First Major Trophy
timeline.description: Eder's extra-time goal defeated hosts France in Paris to secure Euro 2016 glory.

timeline.title: Nations League Winners
timeline.description: Won the inaugural UEFA Nations League tournament on home soil, defeating the Netherlands.
